cvEn:
Zohar (Sonale) Linik, eldest son of Maya and Mordehai, was born on 8 Adar 5709 (9 March 1949) in Yehud. He completed his first elementary school studies at the David Remez Elementary School there, and afterward studied at the Hof HaSharon educational institution at Kibbutz Yakum.

He was a member of Hashomer Hatzair and led a group at the youth branch of the movement in Kiryat Haim. From his earliest childhood he showed a gift for leadership and was an example of integrity and honesty. According to his many friends and the youngsters he guided, this was the finest period of his life.

Zohar loved nature and photography, and he even organized trips and excursions. His camera was with him wherever he went on the paths of the homeland, and he captured landscapes and experiences through it. While still in elementary school he played the violin, but over time he switched to the trumpet, and in his teenage years he expressed his feelings through the harmonica. He had a stormy, restless temperament, yet by nature he was also self-controlled and kept to himself. In dance and drama he reached an artistic level. He was kind-hearted and ready to help others.

He prepared for his service in the IDF, and when he was drafted in August 1967 he became a brother and an example to his friends. Shortly before his enlistment he said that personally he was ready to give everything to the IDF. On 25 Adar 5728 (25 March 1968) he fell while performing his duties. He was laid to rest in the military cemetery at Kiryat Shaul.

In the short time he served, he proved himself to be physically fit and resourceful. He was serious, as evidenced by the serious books he liked to read in his free time. In a letter of condolence to his parents, his unit commander wrote: "Zohar served in my unit for only about three months, so I did not have the chance to get to know him well. But I want to note that about a year ago I interviewed a very large number of candidates for conscription, and among them was your son. Out of more than one hundred and fifty who volunteered for my unit, I chose a small number of soldiers, and Zohar was among them. I think this fact speaks for itself and proves his character and qualities. During Zohar's service in the unit, he stood out for his fine qualities as a soldier and as a person, and he was loved by his fellow team members and by his immediate commander."
